slides.title: Plan of a C++ repository
slides.subtitle: From a pile of files to a repo anyone can build
slides.notes: Introduce yourself, say what the audience will be able to do at the end.

slides.title: Why a plan
slides.notes: Ask the room how they start on an unknown project: someone clones the repo, what do they need?

slides.title: What a newcomer needs
slides.notes: Four questions, in this order: wait for the answer before showing the next. Where is what: sources, headers, tests, docs.

slides.label: command from clone to build
slides.notes: The goal of the whole talk: one command, nothing to ask anyone.

slides.title: CMake describes, Make runs
slides.notes: CMake describes the project once and generates the build of each platform; keep make as a thin wrapper so the commands people expect still work.

slides.title: The tools of the repo
slides.notes: One logo per tool, one tool per need: the language, the build, the history, the checks on a clean machine.

slides.title: One command per need
head: Need
Tool
Command
slides.notes: Every row is one command to remember.

slides.title: Clone, then one command
slides.notes: make calls CMake with the right folders; the binary lands at the root of the repository.

slides.title: A minimal CMakeLists
slides.code:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(myproject VERSION 1.0.0)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
add_executable(myproject src/main.cpp)
slides.notes: Point at the version line: the project version is written once and reused everywhere.

slides.title: The path of a change
slides.notes: Write the code; the hooks run the style and the tests; the CI builds on a clean machine. The machine checks, not the reviewer.
